newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies close mostly lower as G7 meets.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies close mostly lower as G7 meets.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed lower in lackluster trade, as the overall forex market reacted very little to U.S. and Japanese comments at the start of the Group of Seven's three-day meeting, traders and analysts said.
The forex market appeared to obey Japanese finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka and U.S. Treasury secretary Robert Rubin's comments that excessive currency volatility was undesirable.
Mitsuzuka and Rubin spoke of their agreement at a bilateral meeting ahead of the G7 summit in Denver. September yen fell, but remained above the week's low at $0.008730.

"If you put all the comments together, they are pretty status quo," Michael Malpede, senior currency analyst at Refco Inc, said. "It seems as though they are bending over backward to keep the dollar from reacting."
September yen downticked after a Japanese spokesman said Japan is "sincere" in its efforts to deregulate its economy.
The contract fell to $0.008809, holding above the weekly low of $0.008730 that was hit last Thursday.
"The deregulation pact is the most significant and should put short-term pressure on yen," Malpede said.
Japan this week agreed to allow the U.S. to participate in future discussions on deregulating key sectors of Japan's economy.
Washington hopes the structural changes in Japan's markets will reduce the growing U.S.-Japanese trade imbalance.
Japan's economic reform measures could also attract foreign capital in the long term and lift the yen. Some analysts look September yen to test $0.009370, or 108.00 spot yen, in the long term.
Resistance rests at the 6-1/4-month high of $0.009174.
Like yen futures, September marks and Swiss francs drifted lower in rangebound trade.
"There are some people trying to pick bottoms, but I think that is premature," Malpede said.
Sterling futures ended higher after September rose towards the four-week high of $1.6550.

At the end of pit trade, September yen was off $0.000059 at $0.008826, marks fell $0.0019 at $0.5824, Swiss francs lost $0.0020 at $0.7015, sterling was up $0.0074 at $1.6524, Canadian dollars were off $0.0026 at $0.7226, Australian dollars rose $0.0013 at $0.7524 and Mexican pesos were $0.000025 higher at $0.121150. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
